title: "China's national emissions trading scheme"
---

::: {.stand}
Last checked: 13 Oct 2026
:::

## Overview

China's national emissions trading scheme started trading in July 2021, covering the power sector [@mee_qa_2025]. It is administered by the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE).

## 2025 extension: steel, cement, aluminium

The work plan of March 2025 brings three industrial sectors into the scheme [@mee_2025]:

| Sector | Gases covered |
|---|---|
| Steel | CO₂ |
| Cement | CO₂ |
| Aluminium smelting | CO₂, CF₄, C₂F₆ |

According to the MEE, this adds around **1,500 companies** and around **3 billion t** of emissions; the market then covers **more than 60 % of national CO₂ emissions** [@mee_qa_2025].

### Allocation and phases

| Period | Rule |
|---|---|
| 2024 (first compliance year) | Allocation equal to verified actual emissions |
| 2025 – 2026 | Allocation via intensity benchmarks (output-based) |
| 2024 – 2026 | Start-up phase: data quality, emissions management, market familiarisation |
| from 2027 | Deepening phase: more precise allocation, gradual tightening of sector caps |

Source: [@mee_2025]

::: {.einordnung}
**My assessment:** Because 2024 allocation matched actual emissions, the new sectors hardly needed to buy allowances on balance for that year. This matters for the [CBAM deduction](schnittstellen.qmd).
:::
